entry.title: Histoire de la Macédoine hellénistique
entry.summary: Cette bibliographie propose une entrée en matière progressive au non-spécialiste intéressé à l’histoire du royaume de Macédoine, région du nord de la Grèce dont Alexandre le Grand est le symbole et le souverain le plus célèbre. Elle se focalise sur la période hellénistique du royaume : moins, donc, sur le règne d’Alexandre lui-même (336-323 avant notre ère) que sur l’époque nouvelle qu’il ouvre, dont les acteurs essentiels pour la Macédoine sont les rois de la dynastie antigonide, qui occupe le trône pendant la plus grande partie de cette époque (277-168 avant notre ère). Les références proposées traitent d’abord d’histoire politique, mais cherchent à couvrir aussi toutes les problématiques d’une société (économie, guerre, religion, culture…) et tous les documents par lesquels on l’étudie (sources littéraires, archéologiques, numismatiques, épigraphiques…).

entry.title: Journal of Ancient Civilizations (JAC), or How to place an Afro-Eurasian antiquity journal in the scholarly market
entry.summary: This paper delineates the development of the Journal of Ancient Civilizations (JAC) — published by the Institute for the History of Ancient Civilizations (IHAC), Northeast Normal University, Changchun, China — and its contributions to the scholarly world. JAC has transformed from an institute's network-based platform into an internationally recognized scholarly publication which serves to bridge the gap between Chinese scholars studying the Ancient Afro-Eurasian world and the latest international research. This paper reviews the transformation process and addresses the challenges currently being faced by the integrated institution-journal-identity model in a rapidly changing journal market which trends towards digital publishing.

entry.title: Ancient Egyptian Kingship
entry.summary: This guide introduces readers to the fundamentals, essential developments, and complementary developments of ancient Egyptian kingship studies. Ancient Egyptian kingship, a complex facet of ancient Egyptian society, remains a topic of fascination for both scholars and the wider public. Its study has traditionally focused on the nature of kings and related topics such as legitimacy and cosmology. However, in recent years scholars have started to recontextualize kingship within broader ancient Egyptian society, seeking to understand how the royal institution was engaged with by a variety of actors. This guide traces some of these developments and provides readers with an overview of the origins of scholarship and the current state of the field.

entry.title: Dealing with ancient Egyptian mortuary texts: why and how to study an ancient culture in the 21st century
entry.summary: Ancient Egyptian mortuary texts are ad-hoc, in-context productions that were in constant adaptation to changes in mentality, specific production situations, and use interests, rather than established textual units. For this reason, their variability is so high that the need for digital techniques to assess this fundamental feature is evident to anyone familiar with this material. This article briefly presents the problems, aims, and strategies proposed by the MORTEXVAR project and related projects run at the University of Alcalá.

entry.title: Bibliographie essentielle sur Platon et l’Égypte
entry.summary: L’objectif principal de cet article est d’offrir un accès rapide à une bibliographie essentielle sur l’Égypte chez Platon. En effet, cette thématique n’est abordée que dans un champ d’études très restreint qui fréquemment passe sous silence. Cela concerne autant l’historicité du voyage de Platon en Égypte que le débat autour de la pensée égyptienne. Dans ce dernier cas, s’il y a des mentions explicites dans les dialogues, on ne doit pas ignorer qu’il y a également des traces implicites, encore moins débattes. On soulignera, brièvement, le mythe de l’Atlantide, la critique de l’écriture dans le mythe de Theuth et d’autres thèmes tels que l’eschatologie, la politique et les arts.

entry.title: L'Amérique face aux pharaons : l'égyptomanie américaine au XIXe siècle
entry.summary: Ce guide bibliographique propose une synthèse structurée des travaux consacrés à l’égyptomanie américaine entre la fin du XVIII e siècle et la fin du XIX e siècle. Il vise à organiser un champ de recherche en plein essor, relatif à la réception de l’Antiquité, en mettant en lumière la diversité des approches historiques, culturelles, politiques et intellectuelles mobilisées pour étudier la fascination américaine autour de l’Égypte antique.

entry.title: Building an OPAC for a Specialized Ancient Near Eastern and Egyptological Library in Japan: The UTsukuba RCWAC OPAC
entry.summary: This paper describes the design, implementation, and deployment of a quadrilingual (Japanese, English, Arabic, German) open-source Online Public Access Catalogue (OPAC) for the Research Center for West Asian Civilization (RCWAC) at the University of Tsukuba. The RCWAC library holds over 9,000 volumes spanning cuneiform studies, West Asian archaeology, and Egyptology, including donated collections of considerable scope. Faced with the challenge of making this multilingual, multiscript collection discoverable without dedicated server infrastructure or institutional IT support, we developed a fully client-side single-page application built with Vite, powered by Zotero RDF data, and deployed at zero cost on GitHub Pages and a university Apache server. The system features token-based fuzzy search with optional semantic similarity via ONNX Runtime Web, a four-section transliteration keyboard for Egyptological and Assyriological special characters, right-to-left layout support for Arabic, and prominent call number display to bridge digital discovery with physical shelf access. By situating this project within the broader landscape of digital library platforms for ancient studies—from large-scale initiatives such as the Cuneiform Digital Library Initiative (CDLI) and the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (TLA) to the Lib-Static methodology for sustainable digital collections—we discuss the practical choices, technical trade-offs, and lessons learned that may inform similar efforts at other specialized research libraries.

entry.title: Egyptological and Ancient Near Eastern Studies in Japan: Key References Available in Japanese Libraries
entry.summary: This bibliographic guide surveys the principal Japanese-language publications and reference works for Egyptological and Ancient Near Eastern studies that are available primarily or exclusively in Japanese libraries, with particular attention to the holdings of the Research Center for West Asian Civilization (RCWAC) library at the University of Tsukuba. It covers pioneering grammars and textbooks, institutional histories, and key serial publications that have shaped the development of Orientogaku in Japan from the early twentieth century to the present. 本書誌ガイドは、主に日本国内の図書館でのみ利用可能なエジプト学・古代近東研究の日本語文献および参考資料を概観するものである。筑波大学西アジア文明研究センター(RCWAC)図書室の蔵書に特に注目しつつ、20世紀初頭から現在に至るまで日本のオリエント学の発展を形作ってきた先駆的文法書・教科書、学術史、主要逐次刊行物を取り上げる。

entry.title: Bibliothèque ouverte des mondes anciens (BOMA): Initial Milestones of an Independent Open-Access Non-Profit Publishing Initiative
entry.summary: Bibliothèque ouverte des mondes anciens (BOMA) is a non-profit publishing initiative conceived in France during the summer of 2025. This paper presents the initial milestones reached after several months of development. It describes the two foundational pillars of BOMA: 1) a zero-cost operating model and 2) an editorial policy that encourages experimentation. It discusses the legal framework, hosting and indexation, long-term online preservation, licensing, scientific authority, publishing tools, and visual identity, before outlining future perspectives.

entry.title: Egyptology and Social Media: the YouTube Experience Initiative
entry.summary: Ancient Egypt, and Egyptology by extension, have long been popular subjects and field of study. Exhibitions, documentaries, books, artistic productions… Whenever Ancient Egypt is presented, the general public is drawn to it, or at least intrigued by it. From a more positive perspective, we can consider that this popularity is a great way to spread knowledge about Egyptian civilization. Nonetheless, as light means shadow, this popularity has always fostered the emergence of conspiracy theories, fake revelations, ideological fights, and so on. Social media intensified this state of affairs, especially since Egyptologists have been late taking on this new medium, thus allowing people with varying degrees of malicious intent to occupy this space without being challenged or debunked. This paper aims to explain why and how I created a YouTube channel dedicated to Egyptology, and to present the conclusions I drew from this experience, both regarding Egyptology itself, as an academic field, and its relationship with the public. I will discuss the effectiveness of this practice, as well as its limitations, and what we can expect from the future of popularization of science, particularly History.

entry.title: Public Outreach through Serious Games: The Case of ArchéoSport
entry.summary: Public outreach aims to make scientific knowledge accessible to the widest possible audience by fostering exchange, understanding and critical thinking. Among the innovative tools currently being used, serious games are playing an increasingly prominent role, thanks to their ability to combine learning and entertainment. By drawing on experimentation, motivation, social interaction and learning from mistakes, they enable participants to engage actively with knowledge. The game ArchéoSport, developed at the Université de Montpellier Paul-Valéry, illustrates this approach. Created as part of research into the archaeology of sport and the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, it invites participants to explore the evolution of sporting practices from the Neolithic period to the contemporary era. Using a timeline and cards depicting archaeological artefacts, players identify, date and interpret remains associated with ancient physical activities. Beyond the history of sport, the game raises awareness of archaeological methods, develops critical thinking, and addresses social issues such as the role of women, disability, and the religious, political and educational functions of sport. Developed collaboratively by researchers, museums and sports institutions, ArchéoSport demonstrates the potential of serious games as tools for public outreach. Despite the challenges involved in their design and in assessing their impact, such initiatives offer an effective approach to strengthening scientific literacy and bringing research closer to society.

entry.title: A Year in the Life of Science Factory: Digital Outreach and Academic Networks in Public Egyptology
entry.summary: This paper analyses the trajectory and development of the social media channel and videopodcast Science Factory during its first year of activity. After more than ten years, La Fábrica de la Ciencia, a Spanish-language video podcast, created an internationally oriented multilingual section. Unexpected technical issues associated with the production of the international interviews led to the creation of an independent platform: Science Factory. Although initially conceived as a twin project, the two channels soon diverged. Whereas La Fábrica de la Ciencia continued to cover a broad range of scientific topics, Science Factory became exclusively dedicated to Egyptology. The content was structured around three main areas: archaeological field work, museum work and academic research. This paper examines the development of Science Factory as both a digital outreach initiative and a case study in public archaeology and science communication. The analysis is based on a database compiled from YouTube analytics collected during the study period (between March 2025 and March 2026), allowing us to evaluate patterns, audience behaviour and content performance. The results suggest the following ideas: the first one shows that the project’s academic networks were essential for establishing its credibility and facilitating access to internationally recognized specialists; and the second one illustrate that quantitative analysis proves that short and long-form interviews, rather than competing with one another, fulfil complementary functions: Shorts increased discoverability, while interviews promoted deeper engagement with Egyptological research. The study argues that digital outreach should itself be considered an object of scholarly research. Systematic analysis of platform metrics provides valuable evidence for understanding how specialized archaeological knowledge circulates beyond academia and offers practical insights for the development of future outreach initiatives, including the successor project Egyptology Now.

entry.title: Exhibition TA-MERI: Terra Amada. Combining Art, Academic Knowledge and Artificial Intelligence
entry.summary: This paper explores interdisciplinarity in the production of knowledge, highlighting the fusion of theoretical reflection, contemporary painting and artificial intelligence. The exhibition TA-MERI: Terra Amada (TA-MERI: Beloved Land) served as a practical model illustrating how collaboration between Egyptologists, painters and multimedia engineers can create new forms of cultural, artistic and pedagogical communication in the twenty-first century, thereby broadening the dissemination of research and the reception of ancient Egypt.

entry.title: Setting Ancient Egyptian Poetry to Music, Then Getting Montpellier Middle Schoolers to Sing in Ancient Egyptian
entry.summary: The article presents NASHAQ and a Montpellier workshop where students explore Ancient Egyptian poetry, Eastern Mediterranean rhythms, writing systems, and multilingual song composition, linking artistic creation, cultural mediation, and our heritage.
